name: AP website on AI in news production, training and reporting
title: AP website on AI in news production, training and reporting
answer: The Associated Press website gathers AP's own reporting and product pages on artificial intelligence in news. Its most useful material for media readers is AP's account of how it deploys AI in news gathering, production and distribution, including video shotlists reviewed by editors, English to Spanish article translation with human oversight, summaries, Merlin visual search, and five Local News AI projects with local outlets. It also offers the AP Stylebook's AI chapter and training resources. The site mixes these operational details with news features on AI in campaigns, games and elections.

sections.body: The Associated Press publishes ap.org. The pages reviewed include AP news articles from 2024 and a product page titled artificial intelligence solutions. They cover AP's use of AI in news gathering, production and distribution, its Local News AI initiative, its AP Stylebook guidance on covering AI, and AP reporting on AI in political campaigns, video games, older Americans' classes and election information. The material also references AP's 2022 investigative series Tracked and a 2022 report on AI in local news. The pages carry 2024 datelines and refer to projects from 2023 and earlier.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: AP's artificial intelligence solutions page says the organisation is exploring how AI can streamline news production and enhance editorial efficiency. AP uses AI tools to analyse video and create shotlists, with all generated descriptions reviewed and edited by editorial staff before publication, and says shotlists are meant to help customers find shots, not to be republished. It works with AppliedXL to analyse federal registry data and provide news tips to local newsrooms, and with ShortTok on AI-powered content discovery and video curation. Merlin, AP's AI search, recognises elements within photos and videos without relying on descriptions or metadata. AP has rolled out generative AI with human-in-the-loop article translations from English to Spanish and uses AI to generate concise summaries. In 2023 AP developed five AI projects through its Local News AI initiative, funded by the John S. and James L. Knight Foundation. These automated public safety incident writing at the Brainerd Dispatch, published Spanish-language weather alerts at El Vocero de Puerto Rico, transcribed and summarised video for KSAT-TV, sorted news tips for WFMZ-TV, and expanded the Minutes city council transcript app for WUOM-FM. AP also offers training through a Patrick J. McGovern Foundation grant, including tip sheets, LocalizeIt guides and the AP Stylebook chapter on AI, which gives guidance on covering AI across beats, key terms and reporting strategies. AP's Tracked series examined mass surveillance and predictive tools, won awards and prompted a federal civil rights investigation. AP's 2022 report surveyed US newsrooms' AI readiness.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The AP-NORC/USAFacts survey found about two-thirds of U.S. adults are not very or not at all confident that AI-powered chatbots or search results provide reliable and factual information. Public Citizen is cited for the claim that more than a third of states have passed laws regulating AI in politics. An AARP report said Americans over 60 lose $28.3 billion annually to financial extortion schemes. A Game Developers Conference report found nearly half of developers surveyed said generative AI tools are used in their workplace, 31% said they personally use them, 37% at indie studios reported use, and roughly four out of five worried about ethical use. AP says it developed five AI projects in 2023 and that its Tracked series brought together more than 40 AP journalists. The article on older Americans names Barbara Winston, 89, and says instructor Michael Gershbein teaches an AI course once or twice a week.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Media can use this source to see how a major news organisation describes its own AI adoption, including human review of AI-generated video descriptions, human-in-the-loop translation, AI summaries, visual search and local newsroom automation. The Local News AI projects give concrete examples of small and local outlets applying AI to public safety reporting, weather alerts, transcription, news tips and council meetings. The AP Stylebook AI chapter and training materials show how AP is trying to set AI literacy standards for journalists. The news features add context on AI deepfakes in campaigns, AI-driven game characters, seniors' AI education and public distrust of AI election information, all relevant to media coverage of AI's social effects.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Media

sections.body: The pages reviewed do not reproduce AP's full newsroom standards for generative AI in journalism. They describe AP's AI tools, projects, training and Stylebook guidance, but not the complete rules on what may be produced, verified or published. The solutions page is AP's own product and initiative description, so it is promotional in part and not an independent evaluation. The news articles are dated 2024 and earlier, and one survey article is truncated. The source is a mix of news and product pages rather than a single policy document.
